f.title: Health practitioners must report adverse drug reactions to the pharmacovigilance authorities
f.statement: In addition to their statutory and regulatory obligations, medical health practitioners are required to report to the competent pharmacovigilance authorities the adverse effects secondary to the administration of medicines (Art. 177 also requires reporting of medical device incidents to the materiovigilance authority and poisonings to the toxicology authority).

f.statement: Clinical studies must be carried out in accordance with the applicable good practice rules, in structures approved and authorised for that purpose, under the arrangements set by the minister in charge of the pharmaceutical industry.

f.title: Obtain ministerial authorisation before conducting a clinical study

f.title: Every clinical study must have a sponsor
f.statement: Clinical studies must be conducted by a sponsor. The sponsor is the natural or legal person who takes the initiative of the clinical study; it may be a pharmaceutical laboratory, a service provider approved by the ministry in charge of the pharmaceutical industry, a healthcare establishment, a learned society, a research institution or a natural person with the required qualifications and competences.

f.title: Notify serious or unexpected adverse effects and new safety facts within 7 days
f.statement: The sponsor must notify immediately, and at the latest within seven days, any serious or unexpected adverse effect, or any new safety fact, occurring during or after the end of the study, to the minister in charge of the pharmaceutical industry, to the medical ethics committee for the clinical studies concerned and to all investigating physicians concerned.
